messages:
mika: quick FYI, ran a bring-up smoke for gossamer-v3 embeddings on the wiki-holdout (12k queries). overall recall@5 is close but recall@1 and recall@3 for very short queries (<5 tokens) dropped notably. dropping numbers + short diagnostic plan.
oliver: can you paste the exact numbers and eval flags?
mika: snapshot below:
```
baseline: beacon-v2 fp16   recall@1=0.412  recall@3=0.598  recall@5=0.684
gossamer-v3 fp16           recall@1=0.368  recall@3=0.552  recall@5=0.677
gossamer-v3 int8 pchannel  recall@1=0.375  recall@3=0.559  recall@5=0.671
NDCG@5 baseline=0.702 -> gossamer=0.689
mean pos cosine baseline=0.77 -> gossamer=0.73
```
flags: `--model gossamer-v3 --holdout wiki --k 5 --norm cosine --seed 21` vectors saved normalized for cosine eval. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/gossamer/v3/quick/
renee: cohort split? short vs long? languages?
mika: cohorts: shortseq (<5 tokens) recall@1 fell from 0.391 -> 0.322 (-0.069 abs). medium (5-20) and long queries mostly parity. en shortseq dominates the regression.
samir: what changed in arch/training vs beacon? pooling/ln differences? augmentation?
mika: gossamer changes: switched from CLS-token pooling to an attentive pooling layer and moved final LayerNorm location (pre->post projection). training saw heavier doc-level shuffle augmentation.
oliver: did you check embedding norm distribution and sim histograms? could be mean-shift or variance change.
mika: yes: pos sim mean shifted left by ~0.04; pos sim variance increased. embedding norms for short queries decreased on average and have a heavier left tail. UMAP on 3k shortseq+positives shows more spread and some small clusters drifting apart. gist: https://gist.github.com/mika/gossamer-umap-sample
renee: topk overlap? are ground-truth ids still in top5 but lower rank or disappearing?
mika: there are id-flips. top1 overlap shortseq: 0.79 -> 0.61. top5 overlap: 0.96 -> 0.90. so both rank-drop and some disappearances.
samir: try mean-centering (global or per-shard), PCA-whiten (k=64), and per-dim bias-subtract as quick fixes. also run ablation that reverts pooling and LN placement.
mika: quick tests: 1) global mean-center + renorm -> recall@1 improves to 0.345, recall@3 to 0.577. 2) PCA-whiten k=64 -> recall@1 0.351. 3) per-dim mean subtract -> recall@1 0.356. quant impact small (int8 only ~+0.007 vs fp16), so root cause likely model change.
oliver: please run per-channel int8 calibration sweep (symmetric vs asymmetric scaling, percentile clipping) to rule out quant interaction. also produce a topk-id-flip matrix and a tiny csv of 40 failure cases (query, gold-id, beacon-rank, gossamer-rank).
renee: include embedding norm CDF by cohort and a sample of pos/neg sim histograms binned by query length. useful for model folks.
ci-bot: nightly-eval pipeline queued: job gossamer-v3-onboard-20260406-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/gossamer-v3-onboard-20260406-01/logs
samir: if mean-centering recovers a lot, we can consider index-time whitening as a mitigation for Dedicated customers while model team iterates. but prefer a model fix if ablation shows a clear culprit.
mika: plan: (A) run int8 calibration sweep (6 configs) (B) run ablations: LN-back, pooling-back (C) produce id-flip matrix + 40-case csv (D) stats: paired t-test on pos sim means shortseq baseline vs gossamer. kicking jobs now, ETA ~50m for first results. will post interim table when available. thanks all :thumbsup:
samir: if you want help parsing id-flip overlap I can run overlap-heatmap script.
mika: will ping. closing until results land.
